chunks: And from him (narrated) from him, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami, from his father, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "O Sulayman, do not leave the standing (prayer) of the night, for the one who is deprived (of profit) is he who is deprived of the standing of the night."

key_terms.الْمَغْبُونَ: The deprived one / The one who suffers loss
key_terms.قِيَامُ اللَّيْلِ: Night prayer / Standing in prayer during the night

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Qiyam al-Layl in Shia tradition according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes Qiyam al-Layl as a defining mark of spiritual success, warning that the truly deprived are those who neglect it. This instruction highlights the night prayer's role in cultivating divine proximity and self-discipline, a practice deeply rooted in Shia piety as a means of purifying the soul away from the distractions of the day.
